answer: Because every result is re-executed at random by a peer from a rotating pool, a farm pays compute on each identity and still risks the mismatch that voids the payout. Auditors are drawn from unrelated accounts, so a vine of self-dealing collapses when the wrong reviewer takes the task; the hollow of unpaid work stays hollow until continuous uptime unlocks it, and a field of yarrow clones still pays one compute bill per clone.
